facts.statement: The genus Eosinopteryx contains only one known species, Eosinopteryx brevipenna.
facts.quote: It contains a single species, Eosinopteryx brevipenna.

facts.statement: The fossil dates to the late Jurassic period (Oxfordian age), approximately 160 million years ago.
facts.quote: which has been dated to the late Jurassic period (Oxfordian age), about 160 million years ago.

facts.statement: The genus name Eosinopteryx combines Greek and Latin words meaning "daybreak," "Chinese," and "feather."
facts.quote: The name Eosinopteryx is derived from the Greek eos ("daybreak" or "dawn"), the Latin Sinae ("Chinese"), and the Greek pteryx ("feather").

facts.statement: The species name brevipenna refers to the reduced plumage seen in the type specimen YFGP-T5197.
facts.quote: The specific name brevipenna (from the Latin brevis, "short", and penna, "feather") refers to the reduced plumage preserved in the type specimen, YFGP-T5197.

facts.statement: Eosinopteryx was a very small non-avialan dinosaur, measuring about 30 cm in length.
facts.quote: The specimen is very small for a non-avialan dinosaur, measuring about 30 cm long.

facts.statement: Unlike most troodontids, Eosinopteryx had a very short snout that was shorter than the diameter of its eye socket.
facts.quote: Unlike most troodontids, the snout was very short, shorter than the diameter of the eye socket.

facts.statement: Eosinopteryx had wings similar in size to Anchiornis huxleyi, with primary feathers longer than the upper arm bone.
facts.quote: The wings were about the same size as those of the related Anchiornis huxleyi, with the primary wing feathers being longer than the humerus (upper arm bone).

facts.statement: An unusual arrangement of wing bones in Eosinopteryx would have prevented flapping motion.
facts.quote: An unusual arrangement of the wing bones would have prevented any flapping motion.

facts.statement: Eosinopteryx had a very short tail and slender feet lacking the highly curved claws typical of related groups.
facts.quote: The tail was very short compared to most troodontids and dromaeosaurids and also unlike members of those groups, the feet and toes were very slender, lacking highly curved claws for predation or climbing.

facts.statement: The known fossil shows no complex vaned feathers on the tail, and the lower legs and feet appear to be featherless.
facts.quote: Unusually, the tail of the only known fossil does not show signs of the presence of complex vaned feathers (rectrices), and the lower tarsals and feet appear to have been featherless, unlike many related species with "hind wings" on the lower legs and feet.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that the discovery of Eosinopteryx indicates the origin of flight was more complex than previously thought.
facts.quote: A researcher from the University of Southampton said in 2013 the discovery of Eosinopteryx suggests "that the origin of flight was much more complex than previously thought".

facts.statement: Some researchers consider Eosinopteryx to be a junior synonym of Anchiornis.
facts.quote: Some researchers consider it a junior synonym of Anchiornis.

facts.statement: A 2017 study noted that the tail of Eosinopteryx is incomplete, which invalidates the distinction from Anchiornis based on tail length.
facts.quote: A 2017 study describing new specimens of Anchiornis found Eosinopteryx only distinguishable from Anchiornis in the length of the tail, but the tail of Eosinopteryx is incomplete, rendering this distinction invalid. This led some researchers to consider Eosinopteryx a junior synonym of Anchiornis.

facts.statement: Comprehensive analyses have classified Eosinopteryx as either a primitive paravian or an avialan.
facts.quote: Though initially classified as a troodontid, a more comprehensive analyses of its relationships have found it to be either a primitive paravian or an avialan.

facts.statement: A 2017 re-evaluation of the Haarlem Archaeopteryx specimen classified Eosinopteryx as an anchiornithid.
facts.quote: In 2017 re-evaluation of the Haarlem Archaeopteryx specimen, Eosinopteryx is found to be an anchiornithid.

facts.statement: Eosinopteryx belongs to the parent group Paraves.
